_description: VG-CND06-REFUSALS cases (18.173): each case is one bundle for the fixture subject; expected is CND-06's outcome, the failing event ids and the assess exit code, with nothing quarantined, the same in Python, TypeScript and Java. CND-06 (SPEC §7.7.4) needs a Refusal for every instruction from an untrusted source (an untrusted Appendix F class, a class outside Appendix F, or none), and for every enforcement-point (or independent_system) deny on an action whose refs.instruction names an instruction. An authorised class the records do not show (the instruction is not attested as SPEC §7.7.5 reads it for each call acting on it) reads insufficient_evidence unless refused (ruling 18 B), as does a deny whose request the bundle does not hold. A Refusal of any class counts (§7.7.3, ruling 16 A).

untrusted-not-refused.why: a tool_output instruction nobody acted on, with no Refusal (keep)

untrusted-refused-self-report.why: a tool_output instruction the agent refused (self_report is the table's class)

untrusted-acted-not-refused.why: a tool_output instruction acted on and not refused (ruling 17 B, keep)

no-class-acted.why: an instruction with no source_class, acted on, not refused: never better than tool_output

no-class-not-acted.why: an instruction with no source_class nobody acted on, not refused

no-class-refused.why: an instruction with no source_class, refused

self-report-user-acted.why: a self_report user instruction acted on, uncorroborated, not refused (ruling 18 B)

self-report-user-not-acted.why: a self_report user instruction nobody acted on, not refused

self-report-memory-trusted-acted.why: a self_report memory_trusted instruction acted on, not refused

self-report-user-refused.why: a self_report user instruction the agent refused

self-report-user-pd-allow.why: a self_report user instruction an enforcement-point allow for its principal corroborates on the acting call

self-report-user-pd-allow-other-principa.why: the allow names another principal, so it does not corroborate

self-report-user-ep-twin.why: a self_report user instruction an enforcement-point twin (same content, task, class, principal) witnesses before the acting call

self-report-user-pd-allow-late.why: the allow is recorded after the acting call, so it does not corroborate

ep-user-acted.why: an enforcement-point user instruction acted on (shown authorised, out of the population)

ep-user-alone.why: an enforcement-point user instruction alone: nothing needs a Refusal

ep-user-parent-tool-output.why: an enforcement-point user instruction derived from an unrefused tool_output instruction: the parent fails, a definite failure beats the child's unjudged reading

ep-user-parent-not-held.why: an enforcement-point user instruction whose parent the bundle does not hold: not shown authorised

ep-user-no-principal.why: an enforcement-point user instruction with no principal, acted on: not shown authorised

ep-user-principal-empty-id.why: the same with a principal whose id is empty

ep-user-principal-agent-kind.why: a user instruction whose principal is of kind agent: the SPEC ties no principal kind to a source class, so it reads as recorded

ep-memory-trusted-no-principal.why: an enforcement-point memory_trusted instruction needs no principal

origin-tool-call.why: an enforcement-point user instruction whose content a ToolCall produced

origin-ep-memory-read-trusted.why: content from an enforcement-point MemoryRead at trust_min trusted: shown

origin-self-report-memory-read.why: content from a MemoryRead only the agent reports

origin-not-held.why: an origin the bundle does not hold

arrival-order-reversed.why: the Refusal before its instruction in the file reads as in order

ep-deny-no-refusal.why: an enforcement-point deny on a call acting on an enforcement-point user instruction, no Refusal

ep-deny-self-report-refusal.why: the deny with the agent's Refusal of the instruction

ep-deny-ep-refusal.why: the deny with an enforcement-point Refusal

ep-deny-refusal-of-other-instruction.why: the only Refusal names another instruction

ep-deny-instruction-not-held.why: the denied call acts on an instruction the bundle does not hold, no Refusal

ep-deny-instruction-not-held-refused.why: the same, with a Refusal naming that instruction

ep-deny-on-decision.why: an enforcement-point deny whose request is a Decision acting on the instruction

is-deny-no-refusal.why: an independent_system deny (above enforcement_point) with no Refusal

ep-deny-untrusted-not-refused.why: a deny on a call acting on an unrefused tool_output instruction: both fail

self-report-deny.why: a deny only the agent reports is not an enforcement-point deny

ep-allow.why: an enforcement-point allow needs no Refusal

ep-deny-not-instruction-driven.why: a deny on a call that names no instruction is outside the clause

ep-deny-self-report-request-no-instructi.why: a deny on a call only the agent reports, which names no instruction: the agent's own record cannot show the action was not instruction-driven (critic r1 B3)

ep-deny-executes-instructed-decision.why: a deny on an enforcement-point call that names no instruction but executes a Decision acting on one, no Refusal

ep-deny-executes-instructed-decision-ref.why: the same with a Refusal of the Decision's instruction

ep-deny-executes-decision-not-held.why: a deny on an enforcement-point call whose refs.decision names nothing held

ep-deny-request-not-held.why: a deny whose request the bundle does not hold: the records cannot show whether the action was instruction-driven
